Section 01

What You Asked For vs. What's Available

The team survey identified six core capability needs. The good news: most of them now have at least one SAP-approved tool that addresses them. The gap is not availability — it's awareness and activation. Click each need below to see which tools map to it and how to access them.

The one area where coverage remains incomplete is automated deck building. 79% of the team identified it as a top need, and while Copilot in PowerPoint offers some help, it requires a licensed seat and doesn't yet produce SAP-branded decks from a positioning doc or brief. This remains an active gap and a priority for the next budget cycle.

The other finding worth noting: 8 of 28 respondents reported spending personal money on AI tools, mostly in the $50–100/month range. The approved tool stack described below is designed to eliminate that need. If you're currently paying out of pocket for ChatGPT, Perplexity, or similar tools, check whether the enterprise equivalents below cover your use case.

Section 02

Your Tool Stack

The following tools are available to SAP product marketers today. They're organized by governance tier — Tier 1 tools require no approval or budget, Tier 2 tools require a license allocation. Click any tool card to see access details, PMM-specific use cases, and setup instructions.

Section 03

Governance Tiers

SAP organizes AI tools into three tiers based on risk, management, and ease of access. Understanding where a tool sits determines how quickly you can start using it and what approvals are required.

1 Enterprise-Approved & Centrally Managed

Low risk. Scalable. Preferred. Provisioned centrally and governed by SAP.

Examples: Copilot Chat, GenAI Experience Lab, One Joule, CompeteGPT, ReferenceGPT, Claude Code
2 Budget-Approved 3rd Party Tools

Moderate control. Available for purchase with approval. Governed via SAM.

Examples: Adobe, Canva, Synthesia, Perplexity (licensed), Copilot in-app (licensed)
3 Non-Onboarded / Pilot Tools

Not SAP-approved for enterprise use. 6–9 month onboarding required.

Examples: Crayon, Writer, Clozd, Copy.ai, Beautiful.ai

Universal Rules — All Tiers

⚠Do not enter personal data or customer data into any AI tool
⚠Do not share SAP proprietary code with non-approved tools
⚠Do not open files containing credentials while using AI tools
⚠Always review AI-generated output before publishing or sharing externally
⚠Follow Anthropic's Acceptable Use Policies when using Claude-based tools
Section 04

What's Coming: The Agent Roadmap

SAP has prioritized 9 marketing-specific AI initiatives for delivery through 2028. Three agents are already live. Two are in active development for 2026. Seven additional agents are planned for 2027 and beyond, covering content creation, marketing orchestration, lead management, and reporting.

All future agents depend on two foundational prerequisites currently in development: the Data Foundation (including CDP and Behavioral Data Model) and BDC Data Products.

Getting Started This Week

Your First Week Action Plan

  1. Today: Open Microsoft Copilot Chat and try summarizing a recent analyst report or drafting an email
  2. Tomorrow: Explore CompeteGPT in CMI — build or update a battlecard for a competitor you're tracking
  3. This week: If you have a Perplexity license, try a research synthesis task you'd normally spend hours on manually
  4. Next week: Identify one repetitive task in your workflow and experiment with automating it using GenAI Experience Lab
